description: The line plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different layers for various token-precision configurations in KV cache compression, with the x-axis representing four layer ranges—Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, and Layer21-32—and the y-axis showing the relative change in performance as a percentage, ranging from -20% to 5%. The dashed gray line at 0% represents the baseline performance of a 4×tokens, 4-bit configuration. The yellow line, labeled "LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit," starts at approximately -1% for Layer1-4, dips to around -3% for Layer5-12, rises to about -1% for Layer13-20, and ends at roughly 0% for Layer29-32. The red line, "LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit," begins at approximately 0% for Layer1-4, decreases to around -5% for Layer5-12, rises to about -1% for Layer13-20, and ends at approximately 0% for Layer29-32. The light blue line, "RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit," starts at around -2% for Layer1-4, drops to approximately -10% for Layer5-12, rises to about -2% for Layer13-20, and ends at roughly -1% for Layer29-32. The dark blue line, "RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit," begins at approximately -3% for Layer1-4, decreases to around -18% for Layer5-12, rises to about -5% for Layer13-20, and ends at approximately -3% for Layer29-32. The plot shows that the performance of the RULER4k configurations generally declines as the layer range increases, with the most significant drop occurring in the Layer5-12 range, while the LB-Avg configurations show more stable performance across the layers.
